note: measured, not modelled; no acceleration of any kind (spec-decode, prefix-cache, batching) is enabled on this path -- M06 is the separate, later gate for that. GLM's routed MoE means device-resident bytes grow with the run rather than being fixed at load, and cost is content-dependent (different tokens route to different experts), unlike the dense Llama instrument gravity_tps.rs measures. Synthetic pseudo-random token stream, not a real prompt -- it maximizes expert diversity (near-worst-case cache-miss rate) rather than reflecting R0's actual sealed screening-gate behavior (repeated-token collapse, which would cache far better).

verified.desc: verify_hash=true: every newly-touched tensor's SHA-256 checked against the artifact's own descriptor before use. The engine registry's production load path (gravity_engine.rs) always runs this way.

trusted.desc: verify_hash=false: same bytes, no per-tensor SHA-256. Isolates verification cost from unavoidable disk-read + codebook/codes upload cost for a tensor touched for the first time. Not what the production engine path runs -- reported to show the safety/speed tradeoff honestly, not to claim it as the served number.

finding: SHA-256 verification of cold-touched tensors dominates: disabling it cut prefill 4.4x (45994ms -> 10406ms) and median decode 3.6x (6359ms -> 1766ms) on an identical 16-token run. Command-buffer batching of independent MoE-expert matvecs (gate/up/down for all touched experts in one TokenCommandBuffer instead of one commit_and_wait per matvec) was tried first on the theory that ~2500 synchronous single-dispatch round trips per token would dominate; it measured a real but modest 12% win, meaning the actual floor at this artifact size is disk read + hash verification of never-before-seen (layer, expert) pairs, not GPU dispatch overhead. A short run touches a small fraction of 78 layers x 256 experts, so these numbers do not represent a cache-warmed steady state -- they are what a cold-to-lightly-warmed multi-shard MoE artifact actually costs, honestly.
